tagline: North from the Ohio on Indiana's pioneer highway.
intro: The Michigan Road leaves the Ohio River at Madison and runs north, nearly straight, through Jefferson and Ripley counties to Napoleon, on its way to Indianapolis and, a long way on, Lake Michigan. West of the road lies the old Jefferson Proving Ground, where the Army fired its first test round in 1941 and whose northern ground is now Big Oaks National Wildlife Refuge.

Indiana got the right of way from the Potawatomi in an 1826 treaty, a ribbon of land 100 feet wide from the river to the lake. Half the pioneers who settled northwestern Indiana came up it, and in 1838 the last of the Potawatomi were forcibly removed along the same road.

moments.title: Madison
moments.text: By 1850 the river town at the foot of the road was Indiana's third-largest city, and its historic district keeps the major building styles from Federal to Art Moderne.

moments.title: Bryantsburg
moments.text: The village once stood on both sides of the road, until the Army took its larger west half for the proving ground in 1941 and left a handful of houses on the east.

moments.title: Napoleon
moments.text: Laid out in 1820 and named for the emperor, the town has had a post office since 1821, the year he died.
